risks.title: False-positive volume on developer machines
risks.summary: Unsigned binaries with LaunchAgents are common and legitimate on developer machines, and the Apple-only allowlist does not recognize third-party Developer-ID or self-built tools, so they surface as actionable findings.
mitigations: Monitor tier absorbs low-signal items (not shown in detail)
User allowlist (~/.config/counterspy/allowlist.txt) to vet known-good tools
Primary open question for the ABORT release gate

risks.title: Signed / Gatekeeper-accepted malware not re-adjudicated
risks.summary: CounterSpy trusts the Gatekeeper (spctl) verdict; a Developer-ID-signed, Gatekeeper-accepted supply-chain implant is treated as trusted and will not be flagged on signature grounds alone.
mitigations: Correlation + tripwires can still flag it on behavior (persistence/listener/TCC)
Documented as an explicit non-goal in the threat model

risks.title: Root /dev/bpf packet capture of user traffic
risks.summary: Inspection reads raw packets from /dev/bpf as root — a privileged capture path over the user's own traffic that briefly holds the very secrets it hunts.
mitigations: Least-privilege: the cBPF filter is scoped to the single selected flow (host + TCP), not the whole interface
Ephemeral: captured bytes live in memory for the view only; never written to disk without an explicit, confirmed export
Local-only: captured content never leaves the machine (the feedback channel is egress-only and carries no payload)
Never decrypts; TLS ciphertext is not surfaced; readable secrets are masked until reveal (§6)

risks.title: Intercept installs a trusted MITM root and redirects all outbound TLS
risks.summary: Arming `intercept` adds a local CA as a System-keychain trusted root and pf-redirects :443 through a local proxy — a machine-wide MITM. If the CA key leaked, or trust/redirect were left installed, TLS on the host could be silently intercepted.
mitigations: Per-launch consent (y/N, default No); the CA is single-purpose, TLS-only (-p ssl), clearly named in the keychain
Reliable teardown: trust + redirect reverted on exit, panic, and SIGINT/TERM/HUP; --uninstall self-heals
CA key stored 0600 under ~/.counterspy; leaf cache bounded; upstream still verified against system roots
Read-only mirror (no modify/block in Phase 2); secrets masked before any flow is published
pf/keychain edges marked UNVERIFIED — a root smoke test must confirm redirect + clean teardown before trust
